title: Transport warmup and deadline strategy examples for SDKs
creator: Asha Patel
description: Provide concrete, cross-language examples and prescriptive guidance for client-side transport warmup, deadline allocation, and connection keepalive/idle recycling across Python, TypeScript and Go SDKs. Objective is to reduce 95th/99th tail latency regressions caused by cold connections and poorly distributed per-request deadlines while keeping TLS and connection hygiene consistent with Redwood runtime expectations.
acceptance_criteria: Three runnable examples (Python, TypeScript, Go) demonstrating: connection warmup, per-request deadline buckets, and keepalive/idle-recycle settings
Integration test that simulates burst traffic and verifies tail latency improvement with warmup enabled
Docs page and migration snippet added to SDK repos and central Console guidance
Telemetry dashboard updated with new metrics (conn_warmup_success, idle_reap_count, deadline_miss_rate) and baseline against current trunk
design_notes: Warmup approach: pre-establish N short-lived connections per host and send a lightweight probe (HEAD/OPTIONS or small generate request) to populate TLS handshake + runtime connection pools before production traffic arrives.

Deadline allocation: use deadline buckets tied to route intent (interactive-chat=300ms, short-gen=800ms, long-gen=5000ms). SDKs expose per-route presets and allow override via RequestOptions.deadline_ms.
Keepalive/idle recycling: default keepalive 30s, idle_reap=5min for hosted; Dedicated/Private customers can set policy via client config. Recommend jitter on recycle to avoid stampeding reopens.
Streaming ergonomics: prefer proactive multiplexing when supported; for single-stream workloads recommend slightly longer connection TTL to avoid handshake penalty during long-lived streams.
implementation_steps: Draft patch introducing ClientConfig.warmup_connections(count, probe_payload) in python/ts/go SDKs
Add RequestOptions.deadline_bucket enum and plumbing to transport layer; wire into retry/backoff decisions
Add connection pool metrics and expose conn_warmup_success and conn_warmup_latency histogram
Create integration test harness that replays burst traces and measures tail latency with/without warmup
Create docs and code snippets for migration and default values; circulate to SDK maintainers for review
testing_plan: Unit tests for deadline bucket selection logic
Integration test against local inference runtime (fixture) to validate warmup probes and connection reuse
Load test (k6) that replays production-ish burst pattern and measures 95/99th token latency with stable seed
Canary rollout on internal customers via feature flag for 2 weeks, collect telemetry and error budgets
